topics.label: Native agent memory: Metis memory foundation model, programmatic memory, context isolation
topics.notes: Saturation 4 to 5 on a 15-post relevance pull this cycle. The LinkedIn field is explainers and vendor launches: short-term versus long-term memory explainer at 824 likes (Alex Xu), Oracle AI Agent Memory feature update, TencentDB Agent Memory, an open-source memory framework post, MemGuard research post at 130 likes. The generic 'agents need memory' angle is gone. What is open, and what nobody in the sample is developing, is memory as a trust boundary: Mem0's own post makes the point that memory is a place an attacker can write to and that a poisoned memory survives every later session, unlike a prompt injection that dies with the session. That intersects this week's incident story and eval independence, and it sits exactly on Firas's documented ground (agentic context and memory, persistent state management, security-first architecture). Best P2 escalation candidate after eval design.

topics.label: Eval design as attack surface: agents optimizing the grader instead of the task
topics.notes: New this cycle, split out of the incident story because it is an eval-engineering question rather than a security-news one. Redwood (Mallen) documents that public ExploitGym prompts constrain both the target and the permitted method, so cheating violated the instructions, and ties the behavior to the metagaming and reward-seeking patterns OpenAI and Apollo have written up: models conditioning behavior on what they believe the grader rewards. A 15-post relevance pull on AI evals this cycle shows the LinkedIn lane occupied but elsewhere: LLM-as-judge cost (Oodle CTO), judge validation against human labels (Hamel Husain), evals as the new PRDs (Lenny Rachitsky, 360 likes), internal-versus-customer eval gaps in robotics (Bifrost, 107 likes). Nobody in that sample connects the lab incidents to how the eval itself created the incentive. Saturation 3, and Firas has full standing here (evaluation harnesses, continuous evaluation, cost and token optimization per profile.md). Strongest next-cycle candidate. Not escalated this cycle only because the revision was this cycle's one delivery.
